newsitem.title: INDIA: MERRILL SEES INDIA MONETARY GROWTH, INFLATION DOWN.
newsitem.headline: MERRILL SEES INDIA MONETARY GROWTH, INFLATION DOWN.

text.p: Global investment bank Merrill Lynch said it expected Indian monetary growth and inflation rates to ease.

"Taking advantage of declining interest rates, the government of India has completed nearly 40 percent of its budgeted net borrowings for FY1998 in the first quarter of the year," Merrill's July 25 India Economic Monthly said.
The government has been able to place its debt issues with banks with considerable ease thanks to sluggish credit demand from the private sector, the report said.
If credit demand continued weak, the government could possibly complete its total borrowings by September, it said.

"The point to note here is that since all issues of government debt have been fully subscribed over the next quarter, the government may have to monetize only a small part of the fiscal deficit," the report said.
"This should result in lower monetary growth and lower inflation," Merrill Lynch said.
